title: Cloud Security Alliance CCAK
summary: The Certificate of Cloud Auditing Knowledge, known as CCAK, is published by the Cloud Security Alliance, or CSA, the industry body best known for its cloud controls matrix. It is aimed at auditors, risk and compliance professionals, and cloud engineers who must evidence that a cloud service is properly controlled. Unlike a purely technical cloud exam, CCAK sits at the boundary between assurance and technology: it teaches how to scope a cloud audit, how to read continuous assurance reports, and how to judge whether controls survive the shared responsibility model. Assessment is by multiple choice examination, with an optional practical review component offered by the vendor rather than a hands on lab. It leads to roles such as cloud auditor, cloud compliance analyst, risk manager and cloud governance lead. The Cloud Security Alliance does not publish percentage weightings for the six study areas, so none are shown here. Verify the current objectives with the vendor before booking. This is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Cloud Security Alliance.

beginner.definition: This is a certificate from the Cloud Security Alliance about auditing cloud services. An audit is a careful check that a company follows its own rules and the rules of its regulators. The code is CCAK, which stands for Certificate of Cloud Auditing Knowledge. It is meant for people who check cloud services rather than only build them.
beginner.whyItMatters: When a company moves data to a cloud provider, someone must prove that the data is safe and the rules are followed. Auditors who understand cloud technology are in short supply, and many traditional auditors struggle with it. This certificate shows you can ask the right questions of a provider and read the evidence they give you. It opens roles in compliance, risk and assurance, and it strengthens the position of technical people who want to move into governance.
howItWorks: Learn the basics of cloud service and deployment models first, so the rest of the material has a foundation.
Study the shared responsibility model, which explains which controls belong to the provider and which stay with the customer.
Work through the Cloud Controls Matrix, which is a catalogue of control objectives mapped to many standards at once.
Learn how to read assurance reports such as SOC 2 and how to test whether a control is really working.
Practise writing audit scope, findings and remediation recommendations in plain language.
The exam is a proctored multiple choice test, so review each domain and check weak areas before booking.
beginner.example: Think of renting a serviced office. The building owner controls the front door lock and the fire alarms. You control who on your team gets a desk key and what they keep in the drawers. An auditor must know which of those two parties to question about which risk. If a laptop disappears from a desk, asking the building owner about drawer locks is a waste of time. CCAK teaches you to sort every risk into the right column before you start asking.
takeaways: You do not need to be a deep technical engineer, but you do need to understand how cloud services are built.
The shared responsibility model sits behind almost every question, so learn it very well.
Study the Cloud Controls Matrix mapping, because it is the bridge between cloud technology and audit frameworks.

objectives: Explain cloud service and deployment models and the assurance implications of each
Apply the shared responsibility model to decide which party owns a given control
Scope a cloud audit and select the evidence needed to support a conclusion
Interpret third party assurance reports, certifications and continuous monitoring output
Assess governance, risk, compliance and identity controls in a cloud environment
Write findings and remediation advice that a cloud engineering team can act on

chapters.title: Cloud governance and enterprise risk management
objectives: Explain cloud service and deployment models and how each changes the risk picture
Assess a provider's governance and enterprise risk management arrangements
Apply the shared responsibility model to allocate controls between provider and customer
Evaluate legal, contractual and jurisdictional issues created by storing data in a cloud service
Judge whether a provider's exit and portability arrangements reduce lock in risk

chapters.title: Cloud compliance and audit
objectives: Scope a cloud audit and define boundaries, criteria and evidence requirements
Interpret assurance reports and certificates and identify their limitations
Map provider controls to relevant standards and regulatory obligations
Use continuous assurance and monitoring output as audit evidence
Document findings, conclusions and remediation recommendations clearly

chapters.title: Cloud assurance and auditing in practice
objectives: Plan a cloud audit programme across multiple providers and business units
Interview technical staff and request evidence that genuinely tests a control
Evaluate change management, logging and configuration control in a cloud service
Assess how automation and infrastructure as code affect auditability
Report audit results to technical teams, management and external regulators

chapters.title: Cloud governance and risk management frameworks
objectives: Apply the Cloud Controls Matrix as a control catalogue and mapping tool
Use the Cloud Security Alliance guidance documents to structure an assessment
Compare the consensus assessment questionnaire with other assurance approaches
Adapt an enterprise risk framework so it works for cloud delivered services
Track and treat risks that remain after controls are applied

chapters.title: Cloud security and compliance operations
objectives: Assess identity, access and key management controls in a cloud environment
Evaluate data classification, encryption and retention controls across the data lifecycle
Review logging, monitoring and incident response arrangements for cloud workloads
Examine network and workload protection controls for virtual and containerised systems
Test whether business continuity and disaster recovery plans match the stated objectives

chapters.title: Cloud governance, risk and compliance in the organisation
objectives: Build a cloud compliance programme that keeps pace with frequent service change
Define roles and responsibilities for cloud risk across business and technology teams
Use metrics and dashboards to show compliance status to leadership
Manage third party and supply chain risk through the full relationship lifecycle
Prepare staff and processes for regulatory inspection of cloud services
